cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Secondhand – having had a previous owner; not new.

p.em: Example: Growing up wearing secondhand clothes made her long for original style.

cosy-blockquote.p: Thrift – the quality of using money and other resources carefully.

p.em: Example: Her mother practiced strict thrift to keep the household running.

cosy-blockquote.p: Envy – a feeling of discontented or longing arousal by someone else's possessions.

p.em: Example: She felt a touch of envy seeing friends wearing original dresses.

cosy-blockquote.p: Hand-me-down – a garment or other item that has been passed on.

p.em: Example: Wearing hand-me-down coats built a humorous sense of pride.

cosy-blockquote.p: Bargain – a thing bought or offered for a low price.

p.em: Example: Finding a unique vintage bargain in a market can be thrilling.

cosy-blockquote.p: Luxury – the state of great comfort and extravagant living.

p.em: Example: She dreamed of one day enjoying authentic luxury and brand-new fashion.

cosy-blockquote.p: Imitation – a thing intended to simulate or copy something else.

p.em: Example: Wearing imitation pearls felt cheap compared to the real thing.

cosy-blockquote.p: Antique – a collectible object such as a piece of furniture or jewel.

p.em: Example: Her father owned a small shop filled with old antique treasures.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gossip – casual or unconstrained conversation or reports.

p.em: Example: Neighborhood gossip focused on who bought new clothes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Pride – a feeling of deep pleasure or satisfaction derived from achievements.

p.em: Example: Despite wearing used clothes, Rose maintained her fierce personal pride.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: I never get nothing → Correct: I never get anything ((Avoid double negatives; pair 'never' with 'anything'.))
Incorrect: Everything I wear is second hand → Correct: Everything I wear is secondhand ((Spell 'secondhand' as a single compound adjective when modifying items.))
Incorrect: She wears clothes from second hand → Correct: She wears secondhand clothes ((Use 'secondhand' directly as an adjectival modifier before nouns.))
